findings.title: RULES.md Maestro Mode [C:10] claims agents are BLOCKED by maestro-enforcer until interview completes — but the hook is registered only under the dead 'Agent' matcher (repo, active, AND template), so the C:10 blocking guarantee never fires in production

evidence.quote:
When Maestro is active, agents are BLOCKED until interview phase completes.
- Phases: recon -> interview -> approval -> execute
- Skipping interview = blocked by `maestro-enforcer` hook

// Only process Agent/Task tool calls
    if (input.tool_name !== 'Agent' && input.tool_name !== 'Task') {

findings.observe_how: Activate Maestro state, attempt a subagent spawn before 'interview complete' — no deny fires; or check hook logs for zero maestro-enforcer PreToolUse activations despite live Maestro sessions.
findings.telemetry: D2b-01 verified the live subagent tool matches 'Task' (Task-matched agent-recall-injector has 78 logged fires; Agent-matched hooks have none). maestro-enforcer.ts:132 already accepts both tool names internally, so the registration matcher is the single point of failure — a one-word matcher fix ('Agent' -> 'Task' or 'Agent|Task') in repo settings.json, active settings.json, and settings.json.template restores the documented C:10 gate.

findings.title: hook-auto-execute.md tells Claude to execute, without asking, ANY bash command found in a PreToolUse deny reason ('The hook already authorized the redirect') — but the named redirects are dead (Agent-matcher split-brain, no hook emits the cited 'Routing to' pattern), and the live denier whose messages this rule auto-executes is smart-search-router, whose suggestions include the banned Explore spawn and a Windows-broken rg fallback

evidence.quote: When a PreToolUse hook blocks with `permissionDecision: deny` and the reason contains a bash command, **immediately execute that command via Bash** without asking.

Run `<command>` via Bash immediately. These are pre-authorized infrastructure redirects (Task→Agentica, Grep→AST-grep, etc).

Do NOT ask user permission. The hook already authorized the redirect.

findings.observe_how: grep -rn 'Routing to' .claude/hooks/src/*.ts returns zero hits (the rule's trigger pattern exists in no hook source); trigger any Grep deny from smart-search-router and watch the rule instruct unconditional execution of its embedded ```bash block.
findings.telemetry: The rule is always-in-context (loaded from .claude/rules/ every session). It converts hook deny text into a trusted no-confirmation command-execution channel, directly contradicting destructive-commands.md's confirm-first regime, and stacks with permission-auto-allow (GAP3-01) which suppresses the OS-level prompt. The 'pre-authorized' premise is false: no Agentica redirect hook is registered and the deny reasons it would auto-run today come from a hook D2b-06/D2b-10 found emitting banned-spawn instructions and an injection-prone broken fallback. Fix: scope the rule to an explicit allowlist of redirect commands, or delete it.

findings.title: sync-known-gaps.md AND manual-sync.md both claim hooks/src/*.ts auto-syncs repo->active — but sync-to-active.sh deliberately EXCLUDES hooks/src ('copying src stomps mtimes and breaks hook-dist-freshness'); the two always-in-context sync tables describe the pre-ddc0641 world

evidence.quote:
# hooks/src excluded: dist/*.mjs is what runs; copying src stomps mtimes and breaks hook-dist-freshness.
SYNC_DIRS="rules agents skills scripts docs"

findings.observe_how: Edit any .claude/hooks/src/*.ts in the repo, commit, then diff against ~/.claude/hooks/src/ — the active copy never updates; only hooks/dist/*.mjs is copied (sync-to-active.sh:128-141).
findings.telemetry: Both rule files load into every session's context. A session debugging an active hook per these tables reads ~/.claude/hooks/src expecting repo parity (it can be arbitrarily stale), or skips a manual step believing src auto-syncs. The remaining table rows (hooks/dist, scripts/ralph, templates/ralph, docs) were verified TRUE against sync-to-active.sh:128-190, so this is a two-row doc fix, not a script change.

findings.title: plan-to-ralph-enforcement.md asserts 'there is no separate hook-enforced approval step in plan mode' and 'The dialog *is* the gate' — stale on the live machine, where plan-mode-approval-gate IS registered on PreToolUse:ExitPlanMode (active-only); the rule is the canonical doc for deciding whether bypass mode is safe for plan workflows and no longer describes reality

evidence.quote: **That dialog is the user-approval gate** — there is no separate hook-enforced approval step in plan mode.
**Recommendation:** for plan-mode workflows where the human-approval step matters, run without bypass. The dialog *is* the gate.

findings.observe_how: Compare the rule's 'Bypass-Permissions Interaction' table against active ~/.claude/settings.json: plan-mode-approval-gate fires on every ExitPlanMode, which the rule says cannot exist. D2a-05 documents the gate's own bypass-mode downgrade bug — the rule should describe both.
findings.telemetry: Three-way split: the rule says no hook gate exists; the active machine runs one; the repo/template don't register it (D2a-08, SEED-15 class). Update the rule to name plan-mode-approval-gate, its D2a-05 silent-downgrade caveat, and the registration drift — otherwise the bypass-mode safety recommendation is reasoned from a false premise in every session.

findings.observe_how: Run the rule's step 2 verbatim from repo root: `python wizard.py` -> 'can't open file ... wizard.py: No such file or directory' (verified absent via ls; actual paths via git ls-files: opc/scripts/setup/wizard.py, scripts/verify-setup.sh, .claude/templates/RULES.md.template).
findings.telemetry: This rule is in every session's context as THE new-machine pointer; BOOTSTRAP.md (the doc it defers to) has the correct flow, so the fix is aligning four paths in the rule. Note the deeper bootstrap problem is what the wizard installs (D2g-01: template resurrects disabled hooks; GAP3-03/SEED-15: template lacks package-install-guard and permission posture) — fixing the command paths makes users reach that flawed template faster, so cross-link on remediation.
